::: {.callout-warning}
## Released workflow, bounded recovery
The core figures describe the reviewed lifecycle introduced in 0.4.0-preview.2
and retained in preview.3. The historical ordinary-publication figure below is
released in preview.3. The separate development-source storage overlay describes
new file-history additions; those are not in installed preview.3.
The exact source and executed acceptance are linked below. This is a bounded
managed-path workflow, not whole-project rollback or a security sandbox.
Use sample data or a disposable project copy.
:::

## Read the figures

| Mark | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **[R] Released** | Implemented in [0.4.0-preview.2](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/releases/tag/v0.4.0-preview.2), within the stated limits. |
| **[?] Open** | An unresolved association; no implementation promise. |

Solid arrows show the reviewed controlled order. Renderers can handle several
documents as one project; arbitrary mixed-language one-by-one scheduling is not
promised. Dotted connections mark an unresolved association, not an execution step.

An **output build** means the production `proj build` path. A **preview** means
`proj build-dev`. Clearing here means final-output clearing, not arbitrary
deletion of project files or preparation of a fresh cache.

## The three stages

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-lifecycle-overview
%%| fig-cap: "Released overview. Open the stage details below for conditions and failure boundaries."
%%| fig-alt: "Three stages: verify setup and run start hooks; clear immediately around analysis when selected; finish a preview or output build with the stated limits."
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false}}%%
flowchart TB
  classDef default fill:#f0f4f7,stroke:#637b89,color:#153b32
  linkStyle default stroke:#26343f,color:#26343f
  subgraph PRE["1 · Pre-build"]
    A["Resolve and verify basic setup"]
    B["[R] Start hooks, then remaining<br/>preparation"]
    A --> B
  end
  subgraph BUILD["2 · Build"]
    C["[R] Conditional pre-clear →<br/>ordered analysis → conditional<br/>post-clear"]
  end
  subgraph POST["3 · Post-build"]
    D["[R] Preview: end hooks and<br/>captured-state restoration; no<br/>publication"]
    E["[R] Output: promotion and<br/>enabled finalization; end hooks<br/>immediately before next-dev<br/>transition"]
  end
  B --> C
  C -->|"Preview"| D
  C -->|"Output"| E
  classDef target fill:#fff3d8,stroke:#8a5b00,color:#342600
  class A,B,C,D,E target
  style PRE fill:#f1f6f3,stroke:#a8bcb4,color:#153b32
  style BUILD fill:#f1f6f3,stroke:#a8bcb4,color:#153b32
  style POST fill:#f1f6f3,stroke:#a8bcb4,color:#153b32
```

The key adjacency rules are deliberate: **nothing runs between pre-clear and
analysis**, or between **successful analysis and post-clear**. Start hooks come
after verified basic setup; end hooks come at the end, immediately before the
output build's transition to the next development version.

### 1. Pre-build details

::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Open: resolution, validation, context and start hooks

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-lifecycle-pre
%%| fig-cap: "Released pre-build order."
%%| fig-alt: "Select root and profiles, validate merged configuration, capture run inputs, preflight targets and dependencies, capture recovery state, run start hooks, then finish preparation."
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false}}%%
flowchart TB
  classDef default fill:#f0f4f7,stroke:#637b89,color:#153b32
  linkStyle default stroke:#26343f,color:#26343f
  A["[R] Select explicit or discovered<br/>project root"]
  B["[R] Resolve profiles and<br/>environment; merge config;<br/>settings HOW / build WHAT"]
  C["[R/T] Validate typed configuration<br/>and explicit resource mappings"]
  D["[R] Capture root, profiles,<br/>mappings, mode and active run<br/>version"]
  E["[R/T] Preflight inputs and exclusion<br/>syntax, targets, dependencies and<br/>enabled Git prerequisites"]
  F["[R] Enumerate and capture managed<br/>recovery state before controlled<br/>writes"]
  G["[R] Run configured start hooks"]
  H["[R] Complete remaining safe<br/>staging, renderer and allowed<br/>metadata preparation"]
  A --> B --> C --> D --> E --> F --> G --> H
  classDef existing fill:#e5f2ed,stroke:#146859,color:#153b32
  classDef main fill:#e7effa,stroke:#315b89,color:#183954
  classDef target fill:#fff3d8,stroke:#8a5b00,color:#342600
  class A,F existing
  class D main
  class B,C,E,G,H target
```

- Root selection, effective profiles, merged configuration and environment must
  agree before analysis starts. The target assigns **HOW** choices to
  `settings` and **WHAT** is selected/run to `build`; this is not permission
  to add unknown fields to the installed preview.
- The captured context fixes resource identity and the active run version.
  In the released implementation, preview retains an existing dev version or uses dev1 of a
  release without writing VERSION; an output run uses its requested release
  version throughout the run and leaves the subsequent dev1 only on success.
- Validate declared paths, script/hook include and exclusion syntax, supported renderer plans,
  dependencies and explicitly enabled Git actions before controlled build writes.
  Probes can have their own effects: this is not a blanket read-only/environment
  sanitization guarantee.
  The malformed-exclusion correction is included in preview.3;
  it fails in this preflight stage, without changing stage order or recovery scope.
  Fallback directory/entry errors also stop here. The recovery
  capture stage reports its own enumeration phase and OS cause before controlled
  project writes. These diagnostics are included in preview.3; ordering is unchanged.
- Start/end refer to the existing pre/both and post/both hook sets, not new
  hook types. Their placement follows the controlled lifecycle shown here.
- Recovery capture must precede hooks and managed mutations. Cache/staging setup,
  supported renderer preparation and permitted metadata/ignore work finish before
  the final pre-clear gate. No new metadata/provenance record is implied here.
- A script's working directory is separate from project identity. Native cwd with
  an explicit project override, safe resource targets and render-context path
  presentation are included in preview.2.

:::

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "Released clearing adjacency. The diamond checks select a branch; they are not extra lifecycle work."
%%| fig-alt: "With no analysis, skip execution and clearing. Otherwise an output pre-clear goes directly into ordered execution; successful execution goes directly to output post-clear if selected. Errors use recovery."
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false}}%%

  classDef default fill:#f0f4f7,stroke:#637b89,color:#153b32
  linkStyle default stroke:#26343f,color:#26343f
  A{"Analysis selected?"}
  B{"Output build, promotion enabled<br/>and clear stage pre?"}
  C["[R] Pre-clear final outputs"]
  D["[R] Execute ordered scripts /<br/>supported renderer plan"]
  E{"Output build, promotion enabled<br/>and clear stage post?"}
  F["[R] Post-clear final outputs"]
  G["Continue to post-build"]
  N["[R/T] No analysis: skip renderer<br/>setup, analysis cleanup and<br/>execution"]
  X["Failure branch: stop success-only<br/>work and use bounded recovery"]
  A -->|"Yes"| B
  A -->|"Explicit empty list"| N --> G
  B -->|"Yes"| C --> D
  B -->|"No"| D
  D -->|"Success"| E
  D -->|"Failure"| X
  E -->|"Yes"| F --> G
  E -->|"No"| G
  classDef target fill:#fff3d8,stroke:#8a5b00,color:#342600
  class C,D,F,N target
```

Preview skips both final-output clear operations, even if an output setting asks
for them. With `scripts: []`, hooks can still run and an output build may export
existing artifacts; that is not proof of complete analysis-free retry identity.

The target routes eligible safe output/data roles and rendered docs through an
explicitly selected versioned cache, keeping configured final destinations
separate. Inputs retain their declared meaning; no undeclared `docs` or cache
mapping is invented. Ordinary scripts can still write elsewhere: path helpers and
staging are **not automatic isolation of every write**.

The selected execution order must follow the supported plan. Do not infer
arbitrary mixed-renderer ordering or RStudio/Quarto R API parity from this figure.

:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Open: promotion, end hooks, version and optional publication

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-lifecycle-post
%%| fig-cap: "Released post-build order with bounded publication/recovery behavior."
%%| fig-alt: "Restore renderer configuration, stage and validate cache artifacts, restore native artifacts, then conditionally promote output. Enabled publication keeps a local release boundary, exports CAS and commits or pushes Git before end hooks and the next-development bump. Previews skip promotion and publication."
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false}}%%
flowchart TB
  classDef default fill:#f0f4f7,stroke:#637b89,color:#153b32
  linkStyle default stroke:#26343f,color:#26343f
  A["[R] Restore renderer config;<br/>stage and validate cache artifacts;<br/>restore native artifacts"]
  B{"Output build?"}
  C{"Analysis and promotion enabled?"}
  P["[R] Promote safe output/docs to<br/>explicitly configured final roots"]
  J{"Publication enabled?"}
  V["[R] Keep successful local release;<br/>close managed recovery boundary"]
  S["[R] Export configured local CAS<br/>destinations, if selected"]
  K["[R] Enabled Git commit / push"]
  D["[R] Run configured end hooks"]
  E{"Output build?"}
  F["[R] Transition to next<br/>development version"]
  G["[R] Restore captured managed<br/>state; retain cache results;<br/>no VERSION publication"]
  A --> B
  B -->|"Yes"| C
  C -->|"Yes"| P --> J
  C -->|"No: including empty analysis"| J
  J -->|"Yes"| V --> S --> K --> D
  J -->|"No"| D
  B -->|"Preview: skip promotion/publication"| D
  D --> E
  E -->|"Yes: immediately after end hooks"| F
  E -->|"Preview: no version transition"| G
  classDef target fill:#fff3d8,stroke:#8a5b00,color:#342600
  class A,P,V,S,K,D,F,G target
```

The end-hook/next-dev adjacency is approved. The released implementation places
enabled CAS export and Git commit/push **before** end hooks and the next-dev
bump. Before publication it records the successful local release and gives up
the managed recovery snapshot. Publication or later end-hook failure preserves
that local release and skips the bump; partial external effects are not undone.
Without publication, end-hook failure still uses bounded managed recovery.
Preview runs end hooks, then restores captured managed state without a version
transition. These are bounded managed-path guarantees, not whole-project or remote atomicity.

Promotion is output-only and conditional on selected analysis and enabled
promotion. Explicit empty analysis preserves existing upload inputs instead;
configured publication may still use them. Metadata means existing project/version operations,
not finished attempt/release identifiers or complete provenance. The implemented
storage path is configured local CAS export; Git commit/push and network checks
are opt-in, not consequences of merely having a Git repository.

An analysis failure does not enter the success-only post-clear/promotion/end-hook/version
path. This page does not introduce an always/finally-hook policy.

:::

## Released settings

| Choice | Meaning |
|---|---|
| settings.output-clear-stage | none, pre or post; default none. |
| pre | Clear immediately before selected analysis, after hooks and preparation. Production only. |
| post | Clear immediately after successful analysis, before restoration, promotion or finalization. Production only. |
| Precedence | Explicit CLI choice → merged YAML → legacy clear-stage environment fallback → default. |
| Legacy compatibility | The existing PROJR_CLEAR_OUTPUT fallback and never/no-clear spelling remain supported; canonical no-clear is none. |

Preview never clears final outputs. Ordinary generated-output clearing defaults
to none; document-output replacement has its own controlled finalization rules.

## Failure and recovery boundaries

The local recovery figure describes the bounded captured-state rule. The separate
publication figure adds the released local-publication boundary; it is not a whole-project
or remote rollback guarantee.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-lifecycle-local-failure
%%| fig-cap: "Existing local failure boundary: recovery covers only captured state."
%%| fig-alt: "Before recovery capture, rejection stops controlled build writes. After capture, local failures attempt bounded restoration and report restoration errors separately."
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false}}%%
flowchart TB
  classDef default fill:#f0f4f7,stroke:#637b89,color:#153b32
  linkStyle default stroke:#26343f,color:#26343f
  A["[R] Preflight or managed local<br/>step fails; also covers end<br/>hooks when publication is off"]
  B{"Recovery capture exists?"}
  N["Stop: controlled build writes have<br/>not started"]
  C["Restore captured managed set"]
  D{"Restoration succeeds?"}
  E["Report local failure; permitted<br/>cache residue may remain"]
  F["Report primary and restoration<br/>errors; retain recovery data when<br/>available"]
  A --> B
  B -->|"No"| N
  B -->|"Yes"| C --> D
  D -->|"Yes"| E
  D -->|"No"| F
  classDef existing fill:#e5f2ed,stroke:#146859,color:#153b32
  class A,B,N,C,D,E,F existing
```

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-lifecycle-publication-failure
%%| fig-cap: "Released publication boundary: preserve local release; do not undo external effects."
%%| fig-alt: "After local success, establish the release boundary, then enabled CAS and Git publication, end hooks and next-development bump. A publication or end-hook failure preserves the release and skips the bump."
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false}}%%
flowchart TB
  classDef default fill:#f0f4f7,stroke:#637b89,color:#153b32
  linkStyle default stroke:#26343f,color:#26343f
  G["[R] Local success; keep release<br/>version; close managed recovery"]
  H["[R] Enabled CAS export,<br/>then enabled Git commit / push"]
  J["[R] End hooks"]
  K["[R] Next-development bump"]
  I["[R] Publication/end-hook failure:<br/>preserve local release; skip bump;<br/>partial external effects remain"]
  G --> H
  H -->|"Success"| J -->|"Success"| K
  H -->|"Failure"| I
  J -->|"Failure"| I
  classDef target fill:#fff3d8,stroke:#8a5b00,color:#342600
  class G,H,J,K,I target
```

The captured managed set is not a whole-project or filesystem snapshot. Cache
results are deliberately retained. Arbitrary external script effects, concurrent
writers, crashes and partial storage/Git effects are outside a transactional
rollback guarantee. A preview restores its captured managed state on success
and failure; this does not make it a security sandbox.

Durable attempt/release records, complete input/code/config/dependency provenance
and safe analysis-free publication retries remain unfinished. Do not automatically
rerun analysis or claim publication was undone after an external failure.

## Maintaining this figure

**Contributor requirement:** lifecycle changes must update this page's diagrams,
status legend and evidence/version references in the same PR. This includes
settings precedence, hook/clearing order, context/version capture, output
promotion and publication/failure boundaries. Link actual event-order and
recovery tests; do not turn a target marker into a released marker merely because
a branch compiles.

Keep the three-stage overview small. Put new detail in the relevant folded stage
instead of expanding one unreadable graph. Render the site, exercise diagram export and verify
the page links remotely; do not require local Quarto/R/Docker builds.


## Failure followed by a smaller build

The controlled order above is unchanged. Remote acceptance now couples the
failure branch to a subsequent successful Git build: real HTML and PDF are
rendered before a later document fails, previous final/native state is recovered,
then a smaller selection is published and its committed bytes are checked.
Retained failed scratch stays in cache; it must not enter the later commit.
Earlier final docs are preserved on failure and replaced only on successful docs
finalization. This is bounded recovery evidence, not a new M2 record or sealing
boundary. This recovery behavior is included in preview.3.


The [storage design constraints](storage-design.qmd) reserve optional future
per-directory DVC delegation. Its restore/build/store integration points and
error boundaries are still undecided; no DVC step is added to the current
lifecycle diagrams. Ordinary native use remains independent of DVC.


The real local-bare-upstream Git tests also check the existing publication-failure
branch: a rejected push keeps the successful local release and skips the next-dev
bump, while an analysis failure restores managed state without a release commit.
This verifies the current boundary without changing lifecycle order, adding a
seal or deciding durable attempt/publication records.


Inventory transition tests exercise explicit CAS calls independently of this
lifecycle. They do not add automatic pre-analysis input or final-output provenance
capture, choose sealing points or complete the unfinished build-record work.

## Source CSV inventory: additional capture points

CSV capture is released in preview.3. Released diagrams above
retain their status. Production with output_run enabled adds these points without
changing clear/analysis adjacency; preview skips CSV capture.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-lifecycle-local-csv
%%| fig-cap: "Current source: production CSV capture within managed recovery."
%%| fig-alt: "Validate history before hooks, capture inputs after preparation, execute existing analysis and promotion, then capture outputs and replace CSV before publication and end hooks."
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false}}%%
flowchart TB
  A["Validate existing CSV history"] --> B["Start hooks and preparation"]
  B --> C["Capture raw / opted-in cache<br/>Save pre snapshot in selected cache when present"]
  C --> D["Existing pre-clear / analysis / post-clear"]
  D --> E["Restore renderer and native state<br/>Promote selected output/docs"]
  E --> F["Capture output/docs<br/>Replace CSV: pre + post + history"]
  F --> G["Existing optional publication<br/>End hooks then next-dev"]
```

CSV replacement remains inside managed local recovery. Publication failure
preserves local release CSV; no remote rollback is implied. Later end-hook
changes are outside inventory, so these records are not sealing.

Configured remote restore is a separate explicit operation, not an automatic
stage in the build lifecycle above. It selects a source, stages a complete
download and then invokes guarded merge/clear installation.

## Configured ordinary publication

Preview.3 publishes ordinary local
archive/latest targets, then the bounded GitHub latest/archive publication path, before
selected CAS export, Git publication, end hooks and next-dev bump.
Configuration/planned names are checked and GitHub routing is frozen before hooks.
Each provider stages every selected CSV snapshot before its first remote mutation;
GitHub preparation additionally checks the remote catalog and shared metadata.
This is not a transaction across providers. Failure preserves the local release
and skips later stages, without rolling back already published destinations.
Preview skips publication. The historical overlay below retains its preview.3 meaning; development-source
metadata additions appear in the separate storage overlay at the end of this page.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-lifecycle-ordinary-publication
%%| fig-cap: "Preview.3: ordinary local and bounded GitHub publication."
%%| fig-alt: "Validate configuration and planned names and freeze GitHub routing before hooks. After local success and CSV capture, keep the local release, stage local targets and publish local data then metadata. Prepare all GitHub ZIPs and validate their remote catalog, upload data then metadata, then continue CAS, Git, end hooks and next development version. Failure preserves the release and reports partial effects."
flowchart TB
  A["Validate planned namespaces / freeze routing"] --> B["Existing analysis / promotion / CSV"]
  B --> C["Keep local release"]
  C --> D["Stage all selected local CSV bytes"]
  D --> E["Local archive/latest data, then metadata"]
  E --> H["Validate catalog/history; stage comparison and ZIP effects"]
  H --> I["GitHub latest/archive replacements, then metadata ZIPs"]
  I --> F["Selected CAS, Git, end hooks, next-dev"]
  D -->|Failure| G["Preserve release; skip later stages"]
  E -->|Failure| G
  H -->|Failure| G
  I -->|Failure| G
```


The ordinary-local publication stage also supports explicit none comparison:
source filenames are uploaded blindly according to the documented strategy
interaction, after all-target staging and before CAS/Git. This does not change
the staged lifecycle diagram or the release-preserving failure boundary.


Ordinary-local latest publication can use the default manifest comparison.
History eligibility is resolved from the already captured metadata and project
CSV; the staged publication position and failure boundary remain unchanged.


The ordinary-local publication stage now finalises archive or latest targets.
Archive comparison eligibility is frozen during all-target preparation; old
versions remain untouched and new versions are complete snapshots. Publication
ordering and the release-preserving failure branch are unchanged.


The ordinary-publication overlay now stages configured GitHub latest/archive ZIPs after
ordinary local finalisation and before CAS/Git. Routing freezes before hooks;
all GitHub ZIPs prepare before uploads, data before metadata. External failure
retains the local release and skips bump; there is no transaction across providers.


Existing canonical GitHub data is downloaded and merged during preparation.
Full uploads precede removal of obsolete empty variants and shared metadata.
Replacement DELETE/POST failures report partial or uncertain state; they do not
roll back remote assets or the successful local release.


No-inspection GitHub strategies select their merge/purge actions during that same
preparation phase. Nonempty purge changes the prepared replacement ZIP; it does
not add an early remote deletion phase or change the release-preserving boundary.


File/manifest eligibility and archive history selection are now part of GitHub
preparation in the current-source overlay. Current and eligible historical ZIPs
materialize privately, then the ordinary local planner computes staged effects;
only those current data effects become ZIP uploads/removals. All GitHub targets
still prepare before the first external write. Metadata-only no-ops and reuse do
not manufacture data uploads; failure retains the local release.


The current-source GitHub stages also have a real synthetic Release witness:
five builds and two restores verified latest replacement, archive reuse/change,
exact shared metadata and preservation of older data. See
[the live verification](remote-compatibility.qmd#live-github-fixture-verification).
No lifecycle order changed for this evidence addition. Preview.3 packages this
ordinary-publication overlay; the earlier core lifecycle diagrams retain their
existing meaning.


A focused regression candidate checks the existing Git boundary: missing push
tracking fails in preflight, while a real commit-hook rejection after successful
analysis retains the local release without advancing HEAD/upstream or bumping
next-dev. It does not change stage order, invent a seal or promise index rollback.

## Development source: writer ownership around the staged lifecycle

This ownership overlay is not part of the installed preview.3 binary.

A build now claims one project writer before input capture and keeps ownership
through validation, hooks, analysis, local finalization, enabled distribution,
Git publication, end hooks, recovery and the next development bump. Normal exits
release the claim. This does not change the stage order shown above or make
partial remote publication reversible. Crashes leave a fail-closed claim requiring
the user to confirm it is stale before removing it.


Pre-publication recovery restores the exact captured version authority, including
development counters greater than one; it does not manufacture dev1. This adds
regression evidence without moving hooks, publication or the next-dev transition.


```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-lifecycle-writer-ownership
%%| fig-cap: "Development-source ownership surrounds the existing lifecycle; preview.3 remains unchanged."
%%| fig-alt: "Claim one project writer before captured inputs, retain ownership through existing stages and recovery, then release the claim on normal exit."
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false}}%%
flowchart TB

  P{"Production local success?"}
  D{"Publication enabled?"}
  L["End hooks; next dev;<br/>observe outputs; retain final CSV;<br/>install completed log"]
  G["Retain snapshot; distribution/Git;<br/>existing finalization; observe outputs;<br/>retain final CSV and log or Git receipt"]
  R["Release owned claim on normal exit"]
  W --> S --> P
  P -->|"Preview or earlier failure"| R
  P -->|"Yes"| D
  D -->|"No"| L --> R
  D -->|"Yes"| G --> R
```

## Development source: snapshot and final Git receipt

Publication-attempt evidence starts at the successful local-release boundary.
The snapshot records possible distribution before provider calls and survives
later failure. Immediately before optional Git, the framework freezes that
snapshot. The normal commit includes it; a later local receipt records actual
Git and end-hook/next-dev outcomes for the next ordinary commit. No bookkeeping
commit loop is introduced. Missing receipts after a crash remain unresolved;
failed requests never promise that remote state was unchanged.

This overlay does not move end hooks, enforce output sealing or change the
released lifecycle figures. Successful plain production builds now install a
completed record after end hooks/next-dev succeed. Previews and earlier failures
remain outside durable-log coverage. Final output observation fingerprints the
post-finalization state; it never silently redefines the bytes already published.


The development-source ownership overlay now observes selected sources, root
dependency declarations and a safe policy summary after preflight, before start
hooks. It reuses existing runner version responses. No hook or version adjacency
moves; startup observations are not immutable executed-code evidence. Earlier
failed-build retention and output-mutation enforcement remain unchanged.

Final observed rows are retained in a checksum-bound per-attempt CSV; the
[history command](cli/history.qmd) reads these alongside terminal records or Git
receipts. This adds evidence without moving hooks, promotion or Git commits.


The existing pre-start-hook startup observation now also binds merged framework
analysis configuration and effective policy using bounded, redacted fingerprints.
This adds evidence at the existing startup node; no hook/version/distribution
ordering changes. The integrated M2 fixture checks success/change/failure/retry.

This overlay adds evidence after existing production failure recovery; it does
not move hooks, output clearing, promotion, publication or version transitions.

Diagnostics use opaque IDs and coarse stages, never copied exception text or

automatic pruning, stronger hook enforcement or crash recovery is introduced.
The integrated M2 driver checks visible local diagnostics and exact last-good
state; real repository tests check Git exclusion and successful-record tracking.


## Development-source registry overlay

The released figures keep their preview.2/preview.3 labels. In development source,
named destination and source-reference validation extends node C in the pre-build
figure, and selected registered/legacy target resolution extends node A in the
ordinary-publication figure. Both occur before hooks or publication effects;
the controlled stage order remains the same.

Registry membership alone neither uploads nor loads credentials. The existing
provider engines receive only selected definitions. Configured restore remains
an explicit separate operation, and registry sources remain available after
removal from the current upload set. Configured local CAS tree publication adds the provider overlay below.
Flat CSV/JSON publication is implemented below; automatic CAS snapshot selection remains deferred;
explicit verification/recovery is described below.

## Development-source storage metadata overlay

Configured local trees add a selected provider at the existing publication phase,
after ordinary/legacy targets and before optional Git. This does not move end
hooks, next-dev or the existing partial-distribution boundary.

Preparation errors before any provider entry retain the pre-distribution recovery
contract. Once a provider may have changed state, no cross-location rollback is
claimed. Preview captures selected local stores and project remote metadata.

## Explicit snapshot verification and recovery

The separate remote verify / remote restore --snapshot operations do not enter
the build lifecycle, run hooks, create attempt logs, distribute data or bump a
version. They select a named store and exact saved snapshot, validate bytes, and
use the existing guarded directory installer only for an explicit restore. The
eleven build-stage figures retain their existing order.

Legacy-flat verification/recovery follows the same separate, explicit path as
tree recovery. Stored-format selection changes no build stage or figure; both
formats use the existing guarded installer and leave project/store history alone.

Flat publication prepares bounded history early, copies raw objects, then holds
the store claim through its authoritative history read/replacement and required
references. All selected raw bytes and inventory bindings verify. Existing
partial-distribution, optional Git, end-hook and next-dev boundaries are unchanged.
The eleven-figure native browser witness remains required.


### Ordinary local file lists in development source

For named ordinary local destinations, the publisher owns a destination writer
claim, reads the authoritative history, and checks the complete staged payload
before replacement. It records actual final bytes and their physical location,
then writes legacy compatibility metadata, new complete history copies, full
snapshot bindings and the small project reference. Failed copies retain honest
partial effects. This addition does not change preview.3 or the later Git/end-hook
ordering; ordinary tree formatting remains pending.


### GitHub file history in development source

After private mirror planning, observe each exact prepared data ZIP or an actually
downloaded retained archive. Stage bounded history/bindings before any HTTP mutation.
Upload data, legacy metadata and the new bundle, checking its originally observed
asset identity before deletion. After every target's required HTTP succeeds, write
all selected project full histories, then small project references. Failures report
partial remote/local effects and retain the local release. Later CAS/Git/end-hook
ordering is unchanged; no atomic multi-target transaction is implied.
